subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which failures and total latency budget should the shared OAuth manager treat as retryable across built-in and plugin-owned providers?
rationale: The single-shot gap is proven, but the repository has no common provider error contract; deciding whether core retries transport errors, timeouts, 429s, and 5xx responses—or delegates that policy to providers—requires auth-owner intent.

options.title: Shared classified retry
options.body: Core retries a narrow standardized set of transient transport, timeout, 429, and 5xx failures within a small total budget while excluding terminal OAuth errors.

options.title: Provider-owned retry
options.body: Each built-in or plugin provider owns retry classification and timing, leaving the shared manager single-shot.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Continue surfacing the first transient refresh failure and rely on subsequent requests, credential adoption, or operator restart.

recommendation.title: Shared classified retry
recommendation.body: Core retries a narrow standardized set of transient transport, timeout, 429, and 5xx failures within a small total budget while excluding terminal OAuth errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared OAuth lifecycle boundary and its adjacent hardening appear to originate primarily in this contributor's merged refactor work.
